title: Lazy Pig
text: Just as promised, we received a commercial passage permit from the envoy of Siltvelt, and so our journey as traveling merchants began. To start things off, we set out the healing items that my Father and I had made and had Keel take on the role of sales clerk. At first, Keel seemed shy and would turn to Father whenever she had a question, but she gradually got used to it and seemed to be successfully making sales without any hesitation.

Slowly but surely, money began to come in. Using that money as capital, we bought alchemy equipment, and my father-in-law gradually began to learn how to make potions. Perhaps because the sight of Yuki-chan and the others—Filolial-sama—is so rare, word of mouth seems to be spreading little by little. They say we’re a medicine-selling caravan pulled by a divine bird.
“Yuki-chan. Could you go a little slower, please? It’s bumpy.”
“Understood.”

Obeying my father-in-law’s orders, she slowed down the pace at which she pulled the carriage, and our journey continued. We’ve actually set a rotation for who pulls the carriage. Yuki-chan, Kou, and Sakura-chan take turns pulling it.

As expected—or perhaps because she’s so eager to be helpful to Father—the carriage shakes much less when Sakura-chan pulls it. The very next day after we started peddling, Sakura-chan’s outfit was ready.

It’s not particularly elaborate—just the kind of clothes Big Sister used to wear. After all, we can’t replicate armor just yet. It’s not exactly the same as Big Sister’s, but the sight of her with two swords sheathed at her waist is somehow pretty cool.
“Motoyasu-kun, are you familiar with the writing system of this world? I should probably learn it too, right?”
“That’s right. I’m learning from my future Father.”

I made a chart of Melromarc’s characters and gave it to my Father. I think it’ll be fine if he learns them in his spare time. After all, it was my Father who taught me the script. I’m sure he can do it if he tries.
“So, I guess there really isn’t a skill for understanding otherworldly scripts, huh?”
“That’s right. I thought there might be one, but none of the weapons that have appeared so far have had that kind of skill.”
It’s not designed to be easy. It was hard to learn, but since it was my Father’s order, it wasn’t a burden.
“Oh well. I’ll just learn it as I go…”
“Boo-hoo!”

Keel let out a disgruntled sound and started working as a vendor in the village we’d just arrived at. Father is mixing potions while keeping an eye on him. Meanwhile, we headed out to gather medicinal herbs found in the surrounding area. After all, buying them up requires capital.

Since Father was stationed at the apothecary, copying down reasonable purchase prices for medicinal herbs, we’re using that as a reference for our gathering. I’ll also be crafting higher-tier potions using my skills. I think we’ve got a decent enough selection. The prices are a bit lower than the market rate, and sales seem to be going quite well.

We can’t even keep up with the demand. There are ways to obtain these ingredients from monster drops, but if we’re found to be carrying them around unnaturally, people will get suspicious. It’s a bit of a struggle that we can’t do that for now. Anyway, when we returned from gathering, Father was beckoning us from inside the carriage.
“What’s the matter?”
“Um… there’s a kid here who wants to join our group…”

My father looked troubled as he consulted me. Join our group, you say? My father has always refused to accept Demi-Humans, suspecting them of being spies or having religious ties. Besides, it’s hard to imagine a human wanting to join a group led by my father. It looks like I’ll have to consider a plan to check this out myself and discreetly get rid of her.
“Oink…”

A pig that seemed completely unmotivated was sitting listlessly on a nearby stump, waiting. What’s with this pig? As I eyed her suspiciously, she let out a low-key oink. …That reaction looks familiar.
“That’s Elena. She’s a noble from Melromarc, and she says her parents told her to come here to lend a hand to one of the heroes.”

Elena? That name sounds familiar. Who was she again? I can only vaguely recall her, but I seem to remember a pig like that being near the Crimson Swine. Kill, that’s it. That’s the only option I can think of.
“Oink, oink, oink, oink…”
“Even if you say it with such a lack of enthusiasm…”
“What exactly is she saying?”
“Um, ‘It’s a huge hassle, but I can’t disobey my parents’ orders…’”
“Well then, shall I just wipe her off the face of the earth? It won’t hurt a bit.”
“Hey, Motoyasu, don’t do anything too extreme!”
Just as I was about to grip my spear tightly and finish off the pig, my Father stopped me.
“Oink.”
“‘So, I figured the Shield Hero and Spear Hero would be the easiest to deal with, so I came to ask for your help,’ she said. What an amazing person.”
This pig shows absolutely no motivation whatsoever. In that case, you’d better head home before you get killed.
“Oink oink oink.”
“‘Well, since my mom runs a business, selling things isn’t exactly out of the question. I can handle that much,’ she said—but still… Keel’s more than enough for that.”
“Oink oink oink!”
Keel’s making all sorts of noises. From the looks of it, he seems pretty open to joining us.

“Huh? Well, relying solely on Keel to handle sales might be tough in the long run. But still… Hey, why did you think joining our group would be the easiest option? As a noble, you should know better—I think it’s actually the hardest, don’t you?”
“Oink-oink-oink… Oink—”
After that, the pig kept grunting at my Father for a while. My Father kindly translated what it was saying so I could understand.

Apparently, this pig has reasons for joining my Father’s side beyond just following his parents’ orders. According to the pig, the Trash faction has a lot of problems with this whole commotion, and staying on their side would likely put him in a bad position in the end. It’d be one thing if it were just the Shield Hero, but his relationship with the Spear Hero isn’t exactly great either. Furthermore, according to the pig’s own intelligence—under the alias “Elena”—it seems the Sword Hero… Ren also has his own reservations about the kingdom.

And since this pig has the backing of one of Melromarc’s leading merchants, it seems he isn’t all that afraid of the Trash’s power. Since his father is a noble who cooperates with the Queen’s side, the authorities can’t go so far as to confiscate his property or strip him of his noble status—at least not for now. As far as his family background is concerned, there’s no issue; it all comes down to the pig’s own preferences.

And what’s even more important, he says, is how well he gets along with the Heroes. The Bow Hero is traveling around the land on what appears to be a “journey to set the world right,” defeating corrupt nobles, while the Sword Hero prioritizes slaying monsters. It seems he’s in a position where he could choose either one. Just then, the Shield Hero began peddling goods alongside the Spear Hero.

So, according to the Pig, from what he observed from a distance, Itsuki can’t keep up with the “righteous” side of things, and Ren usually fights alone—though he does go with companions sometimes—but he ends up being forced to deal with troublesome monsters in all sorts of places. Naturally, it seems only logical that he’d come to us, since our journey by stagecoach looks so easy. I have absolutely no idea what’s “logical” about that, though.
From now on, let’s call this Pig the “Lazy Pig.”

To add to that, it seems it’s important to the Pig that not only my Father but I am here as well. In other words, the fact that not only the Shield Hero but also the Spear Hero is here is the reason the Lazy Pig chose us. Well, if it were just my Father, he’d probably face a lot of public backlash. Actually, I think it wasn’t until a little later in the first world that my Father made a name for himself as a traveling merchant. In that situation, the pig probably figured the other heroes would be a better choice.

“‘Also, once we get through this commotion and the queen returns, the Shield Hero and the Spear Hero are the ones most likely to rise in status…’ is what it said. He’s quite the character in more ways than one. What should we do?”
“Would it be best to just wipe him off the face of the earth?”
“Huh!? Listen, Motoyasu, were you even paying attention? Please handle this as peacefully as possible. We looped back to avoid a war, right?”
“That’s right. Got it. Then I’ll eliminate him peacefully.”
“I mean… oh, for heaven’s sake…”
“Boo…”
“We’ve got plenty on our plate, and we’d be in trouble if he spied on us, wouldn’t we?”
“Boo…”

“Huh? You’d be willing to become a slave just to earn our trust?　“I won’t spy, so isn’t that good enough? In return, if the Queen’s faction wins, I’d like you to put in a good word for my family and country… Well, if that’s the case…”

My father is looking right at me. Hmm… As a slave, he can’t disobey, and it’s possible to prevent him from leaking information. A slave has no voice—I can’t make him reveal secrets… but wanting to join our side so badly that he’d go that far—what do you make of that?
“Boo-boo…”

“Well, we’ve got a lot planned, but it’s true we’re short on manpower. If you become a slave, you won’t be able to lie… All right. I don’t really trust you, but I’ll let you come along. As a merchant, you seem honest enough when you speak your mind, so I guess I can trust you on that.”
“Boo-boo.”
And so, the Lazy Pig joined us as a slave. The inside of the carriage has become even more piggy-smelling.
